info.title: Diffbot Knowledge Graph
info.description:
The Diffbot Knowledge Graph — a crawled, entity-resolved index of the public web (~10B entities, ~1T facts) covering organizations, people, articles, job posts, products, places and more.

Two operations are vendored here, and they answer different questions:

- `dqlSearch` — run a Diffbot Query Language (DQL) expression and get every matching entity. DQL filters ONE entity type at a time with dot-path field predicates; it has no traversal, no joins and no paths. Use it when you want a SET of entities.
- `enhance` — hand over partial identifying data (a name, a URL, an email) and get the single best-matching entity back, scored. Use it when you want to RESOLVE something you already have into a Knowledge Graph identity.

Auth is a single deployment-level token in the `token` query parameter, from https://app.diffbot.com/get-started/. Entity exports are credit-metered, so both operations cost real money per record returned.

get.summary: Search the Knowledge Graph with a DQL expression.
get.description:
Runs a Diffbot Query Language expression and returns matching entities, most relevant first.

A DQL expression always starts with a `type:` clause naming exactly ONE entity type, followed by zero or more field predicates:

```
type:Organization locations.city.name:"Sydney" nbEmployees>500
type:Person employments.{title:or("data scientist","analyst") isCurrent:true}
type:Organization parentCompany.id:or("EU2HJUnMcNoWE3nR1cGBcZg","EHb0_0NEcMwyY8b083taTTw")
type:Article tags.uri:"https://diffbot.com/entity/EYX1i02YVPsuT7fPLUYgRhQ" date>"2026-01-01"
```

Operators: dot-paths for nested fields; `{ … }` subqueries scoped to a nested collection; `or(a,b)`; `not(…)`; `has:field`; `<` `>` `<=` `>=` comparisons; `re:` for regex; `near[30mi](…)` for proximity; `sortBy:` / `revSortBy:` for ordering; `facet:field` to group counts instead of returning entities.

DQL CANNOT traverse. `parentCompany.id:"E…"` is a reverse-index lookup on a denormalized reference field, not a hop — following a chain of owners means running this operation once per level with the ids read out of the previous response.

parameters.name: query
parameters.description: The DQL expression. Must begin with a `type:` clause.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: How to interpret `query`. `query` (default) is DQL. `text` is free-text search. `queryTextFallback` tries DQL then falls back to text.

parameters.name: size
parameters.description: Entities to return, maximum 50. Every entity returned is billed, so ask for what will be read.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Zero-based offset of the first result — the paging cursor.

parameters.name: nonCanonicalFacts
parameters.description: Include facts Diffbot has not promoted to canonical. Off by default; noisier and larger.

parameters.name: jsonmode
parameters.description: `extended` adds per-fact provenance (which source asserted each value). Costs response size; useful when a claim needs attributing.

get.summary: Resolve partial identifying data to the single best-matching entity.
get.description:
Scores candidate entities against the fields supplied and returns the best match with its score. This is the entity-resolution operation: use it to turn a name, a website, or an email address into a stable Diffbot entity id, and use `dqlSearch` afterwards to query from that id.

At least one identifying field beyond `type` is required. More fields means a better match — `name` plus `url` is far more reliable than `name` alone, because company names are not unique and websites are.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: Which entity type to resolve to.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Name of the organization or person.

parameters.name: url
parameters.description: Website or profile URL. The strongest single signal for an Organization — a domain is unique in a way a name is not.

parameters.name: email
parameters.description: Email address. The strongest single signal for a Person.

parameters.name: employer
parameters.description: Person only — employer name, to disambiguate people who share a name.

parameters.name: title
parameters.description: Person only — job title, to disambiguate.

parameters.name: location
parameters.description: Complete or partial address, to disambiguate.

parameters.name: size
parameters.description: Return more than one candidate. Default 1 — the best match only.

parameters.name: threshold
parameters.description: Minimum match score to return anything. Raise it when a wrong match is worse than no match.

200.description: Best-matching entity or entities, each with a match score.

SearchResponse.description: Both operations answer in this envelope. `hits` is the total the index matched, which is usually larger than `data.length`.

kgversion.description: Knowledge Graph build the answer came from.

facet.description: True when the query used facet: and the payload is counts rather than entities.

Entity.description: A Knowledge Graph entity. Shape varies by type; only the fields common to every type are declared here, because the full Organization record alone carries ~180 fields. Cross-entity fields (parentCompany, ceo, employer, subsidiaries, competitors) are EntityReference objects, or arrays of them, carrying the target's id — which is what makes a second query possible.

id.description: Stable Diffbot entity id, e.g. EYX1i02YVPsuT7fPLUYgRhQ.

importance.description: Diffbot's own prominence score for the entity.

nbOrigins.description: How many distinct web sources this record was fused from.

EntityReference.description: A resolved pointer to another entity. `targetDiffbotId` is the id to query next.
